subject: Recap & proposed PoV: dedicated sizing + SLOs for NovaHealth

Subject: Recap & proposed PoV: dedicated sizing + SLOs for NovaHealth

Alex —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed path forward for a short Proof-of-Value (PoV) focused on validating dedicated capacity sizing against your target SLOs.

What you asked for (explicit):
- 95th percentile latency goal for streaming chat responses: <= 220ms
- Sustained request throughput target: 250 qps (average across business hours) with spikes to 800 qps for 10m bursts
- Average concurrency per user session: 6 active streams
- Support for server-side streaming (token-by-token) with acceptable cold-start latency
- Data residency: US-only; will run in our dedicated pool in us-west2

High-level proposal (next actions):
1) PoV duration: 2 weeks of dedicated reserved throughput (we provision dedicated capacity scaled to a reserved throughput target).
2) Baseline sizing we recommend to start: 4 x H100-80GB partitions (quantized FP16) with an autoscale buffer to handle bursts — we’ve included a conservative vs. aggressive sizing matrix in the attached PDF.
3) Load test plan: Redwood SRE will run a controlled load test (scripted sessions, realistic prompt length and streaming) and provide token-level latency distribution and GPU utilization. Dylan’s included some preliminary microbenchmarks attached.
4) Success criteria: p95 streaming latency <= 220ms under sustained 250 qps and no more than 1.5x latency degradation at 800 qps bursts.
5) Timeline & commercial ask: we can spin reserved capacity for the PoV within 5 business days after DocuSign/PO for short-term reserved commit. Soojin — can you confirm what short-term credit we can offer if procurement needs to keep costs down?

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-proposal-novahealth-20260914.pdf (proposal + matrix)

Dylan — can you run the initial microbench (existing model + two quantization profiles) and drop the CSV results in this thread? Alex — would you confirm the primary traffic window (local time) and any non-standard prompt lengths (videos/transcripts, etc.) we should include?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap, and for proposing the PoV. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) Traffic window: primary is 8:00–18:00 PT on weekdays, but we do have international users that generate off-hours spikes up to ~15% of peak.
2) Prompt profile: typical prompts are 50–120 tokens; we have an additional class of long-transcript summarization prompts that average 800–2,000 tokens but occur in ~3% of sessions. For PoV we want one baseline test that includes the long prompts (to validate KV cache and memory).
3) Concurrency: the 6 active streams is accurate; note some background batch jobs will hit the same model for embeddings (low priority).

Procurement: we need a short-term quote and a PoV addendum. Cost sensitivity is real — if we can do a capped credit/discount for the PoV so we can sign quickly that would help.

Subject: Re: Recap & proposed PoV: dedicated sizing + SLOs for NovaHealth

Alex/Jordan —

Attaching the initial microbenchmark CSV and a short technical note. Highlights from the run (local dev cluster; not the dedicated pool):
- Model used: open-llm-34b (close analog to what we plan to serve).
- Quantization profiles: fp16 and q4_0 (aggressive int4-like profile).
- Single H100-80GB profile: sustained tokens/sec ≈ 8.2k (fp16), ≈ 10.0k (q4_0) under perf-optimized kernel.
- Observed p95 token latency (streaming tokens): 18ms per token in the fp16 profile at low batch. Under concurrency 64 streams, p95 end-to-end response latency for avg 100-token prompts was ~160ms on the fp16 run. q4_0 reduced GPU mem pressure but increased variance for long-context runs (800+ tokens) — KV cache churn appears to hurt the int4 path for long transcripts.
- Cold-start: on the same instance, first-token latency under our runtime warm path is ~120ms; cold path (no prefetched KV) is ~320ms. For your SRs where cold starts are unacceptable, we recommend a small standby pool for warm caches.

Sizing guidance (conservative -> aggressive):
- Conservative (recommended for PoV): 4 x H100 partitions (80GB) + standby nodes sized at 15% throughput for warm caches. Reserved throughput set to 300 qps; burst capacity bump to 900 qps for 15m windows (auto-scale policy).
- Aggressive (cost-optimized): 3 x H100 + 1 x L40s for multi-tenant lower-priority workloads; reserved throughput 250 qps, burst 750 qps.

Known trade-offs: multi-gpu pools mixing types can complicate routing for consistent latency; we can route by model-variant to keep strict SLOs on the H100 pool.

Attachments: nova-loadtest-20260913.csv

I can convert the CSV into token-level latency plots if helpful (happy to drop a short dashboard link).

—Dylan
